title: Congressman Pat Harrigan addresses tax policy, AI investment, and defense measures in recent posts
text:
Pat Harrigan, U.S. Representative for North Carolina's 10th Congressional District | Wikipedia
Pat Harrigan, U.S. Representative for North Carolina's 10th Congressional District | Wikipedia
Congressman Pat Harrigan, who represents North Carolina in the U.S. House of Representatives, used his social media platform on July 16, 2025, to comment on several legislative and policy developments.
In a post published at 01:03 UTC, Harrigan addressed recent criticisms from the governor of North Carolina regarding federal legislation supported by President Biden. He stated, "I joined my North Carolina colleagues in calling out @NC_Governor’s baseless attacks on @POTUS’s One Big Beautiful Bill. The bill prevents the largest tax hike in American history, champions policies that result in higher take-home pay, reduces federal spending by $1.3 trillion," referencing key provisions of the legislation.
Later that morning at 11:34 UTC, Harrigan highlighted new federal investments in artificial intelligence and energy sectors. He wrote, "The AI race is the new space race, and @POTUS just committed $90 billion to it through major investments in AI and energy. He is sending a clear message to China that American leadership in critical technology is back."
At 13:04 UTC on July 16th, Harrigan provided an update regarding national defense legislation. He announced progress on an amendment he introduced as part of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 (FY26 NDAA). According to his statement: "UPDATE: I’m happy to report that @HASCRepublicans passed the #FY26NDAA out of committee last night, including my amendment to stop foreign adversaries from operating businesses on U.S. military bases. A major step toward fixing the threat @GNCLiveWell exposed."
The referenced "One Big Beautiful Bill" has been promoted by its supporters as a measure aimed at averting significant tax increases while implementing substantial reductions in federal expenditures over multiple years.
The newly announced $90 billion investment reflects ongoing competition between the United States and China over dominance in emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence—a field widely viewed as critical for economic growth and national security.
The FY26 NDAA typically includes wide-ranging provisions related to U.S. defense policy and funding; amendments like Harrigan's seek to address specific concerns about foreign influence or security vulnerabilities within military infrastructure.
